commands.name: models

deepseekHarness.url.markdownDescription: Where a dsh serves `/api`. The default is dsh's own default bind, so an ordinary `dsh web` needs no change here. The extension **attaches to a dsh already serving this address** — yours, or one another window started — and starts one on that port only when nothing answers. That order is what keeps two harnesses off one `$DSH_HOME`, which dsh does not lock and which corrupts session logs. A remote address is attached to but never started.

deepseekHarness.executable.markdownDescription: Absolute path to your `dsh` executable, used when the extension has to start one. Empty resolves it from `PATH`, then from `#deepseekHarness.checkoutPath#`. This extension never ships a dsh of its own.

deepseekHarness.checkoutPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a built deepseek-harness checkout, used when `dsh` is not on `PATH`. Its `apps/cli/lib/bin.js` is run with `node`.

deepseekHarness.home.markdownDescription: Overrides `$DSH_HOME` for a harness the extension starts. Empty uses your real dsh home, so the editor sees the profiles, settings, credentials and history you already have.

deepseekHarness.historyPageMessages.markdownDescription: How many messages each `session.history` call asks for. **This is not a limit on what is restored:** a reopened session is always read back to the first event of its log, however long it is — this only sets how much of it one call carries. dsh counts messages backwards from where the call starts and returns the whole contiguous range behind them, tool calls, results and token-level chunk events included, so lowering this makes each call smaller and a long session take more of them. `50` is dsh's own default.

deepseekHarness.extraArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments appended to `dsh web` when the extension starts one. The bind host is not configurable: the server has no auth, so it is always loopback. The port comes from `#deepseekHarness.url#`, and is fixed rather than ephemeral so other windows can find and share this harness.
